full_text:
It seems that Exchange C is paid so things have settled a bit. 

The spreadsheet above clarifies the situation going forwards with Exchange B as well as the allocation of funds for Exchange C. This is transparent for those two exchanges, at least, I think I personally understand it.

However, the calculations for the funds allocated for Exchange A are still problematic - or at least - the information in the spreadsheet does not explain the full allocation of the funds.
Although this happened in the past, it needs to be made transparent. The point of this post is neither to point a finger at anyone in particular, nor to claim there have been any mispractice. Yet without any detail and considering only inputs and outputs in the best case scenario, we already see that a significant part of the funds is missing.

Below I will attempt to detail the state of my current understanding. For this, I would like to keep most all the calculations regarding to exchange B and C out of the loop excepted for two transactions: 
1.  A transaction of $100k from the funds of B/C to pay for the market making of exchange A reflected in the spreadsheet.
2. [A transaction of 4,545,454EDG](https://edgeware.subscan.io/extrinsic/0x161155b8e4ca9c0192106f712164b1ec68bce3c95f23f1d9df8d11d34f71e9ad) from the treasury to the MM wallet for Exchange A. This is to meant to cover the market making for Exchange B, where the Market Maker wallet for Exchange A was re-used, as per [this post](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/1004-proposal-exchange-b-edg?comment=2400). 


We all know that there were two proposals for A, and that part of the remaining funds in [the multisig](https://gnosis-safe.io/app/#/safes/0x0a13c5A019955d5bdfdE78F15c377DdE38B3eA42/transactions) will be used for Exchange B and C in return, but this is irrelevant information at this point: at the time of writing the remaining funds are still in the multisig, I am only interested in the inputs and outputs of [the Exchange A proposals](https://commonwealth.im/edgeware/proposal/discussion/827-proposal-top-15-exchange-by-cmc-integration-exchange-a) as a black box. 

So what are the inputs of the proposals: 35.5M EDG via two payments of 21M and 14.5M EDG respectively for market making and integration. The breakdown of the purpose does not matter at this point: we know from the proposal that those 35.5M EDG represent between 1.2x and 1.7x times the total integration+MM costs. What it means is that, even without the breakdown, we know that the real total cost is between 20.8M EDG (if the multiplier was 1.7x), and 29.5M EDG (for a multiplier of 1.2). 
This means that the funds sent through the proposal were enough to cover the full exchange A amount, and that there should be an additional remainder of between 6M and 14.7M EDG in the wallet after all payments are closed.

However, Thom explained that he needed to use $100K of the funds from Exchange B/C to account for Exchange A's marketing costs: see point 1. above. Now as per point 2. above, we also know that an additional 4.5M EDG has been sent to the MM wallet.

This means that the remaining funds from the whole Exchange A transactions ought to be at least $100K (since this is what has been topped by Thom, and we know the treasury fully covered all costs with the Two proposals for Exchange A) and 10.5M (6M+4.5M) to 19.2M (14.7M+4.5M) EDG (from the fact that there was a hiding buffer, and adding the 4.5M EDG of point 2 as they should remain from the wallets too since the procedure for paying Exchange B has not started).

But concretely, in the Gnosis Safe wallet, only 75K USD remain, while in the two EDG wallets, only 5M remain. So without even considering exchange rates, the real cost of Exchange A, etc. It seems we are already short at least $25k and 5.5M EDG. This is in the best case (by "best case" I mean that this is assuming the remainder should be minimal, so it is the absolute minimal amount we lost track from, but the amount could be bigger). Those sums are non trivial and cannot come from the slippage, they have to be found back. 

Once this is clarified, it will be time to audit the exact rates etc. which can bring further differences to explain. Some of the CW Labs members, Thom, and maybe other councillors involved in the multisig may have been made aware of the real costs and their contribution shall be required to understand the inside details. 
Yet, considering the absolute best case scenario, i.e. the minimal amount of what should be remaining without dealing with the inside details, the fact that we lost track of such important amounts is a major concern.

Thom, we all know you have not been responsible for the process with Exchange A, but since you are probably now in possession of most of the details, I think you can be instrumental in clarifying the situation and tracing back the missing funds. Those are very important and they can also help us accelerate the payments for Exchange B.
